segments.caption: An elderly man, wearing glasses and a cap, is shown in his backyard. He is seen up close, then walks away from the camera down a path toward a wooden fence, passing by beehives and a white SUV parked nearby.
A beekeeper walks toward his beehives in a sunny backyard, then lifts the lid of one hive to inspect the frames inside, revealing the busy bees and honeycomb.
A beekeeper lifts the lid of a beehive, revealing a frame densely populated with bees actively tending to honeycomb cells, showcasing the hive's vibrant, living interior.
A beekeeper tends to his hives, inspecting frames teeming with bees and honeycomb, while his apiary, marked with “Stokesberry 1702,” stands ready under the sun.

An elderly beekeeper, Dave Stokesberry, is shown in his garden, observing and tending to his active beehive. The video captures him in his outdoor apiary, with close-up shots of bees bustling around the hive entrance, highlighting the daily activity and care involved in beekeeping.
A beekeeper at Stokesberry Hives in Puyallup, Washington, demonstrates his craft by showing off his honey, pouring a sample from a small dish into a jar to highlight its quality.

An elderly beekeeper is shown in his backyard, carefully inspecting his beehives. He holds up a lid to reveal the honeycomb and honey inside, then examines a small, mesh-covered tool, likely for hive inspection or management. The video captures his focused, hands-on work tending to his bees in a sunny, residential garden setting.

A beekeeper, identified as Dave, is shown tending to his beehives in a backyard setting. He carefully lifts the lids off the wooden hives to inspect the frames inside, revealing the bees and honeycomb. The segment concludes with closing credits acknowledging Dave and his community, as well as the cinematographer, Jack D. Hubbard.
